Clarification needed on Trump's "Pro-Life" stance:

  • He is personally against abortions.

  • He has only mentioned that he thinks abortions should be banned after a certain point, namely once the fetus is viable outside the womb, which is completely in-line with current US Law on the matter. Worst you can say about his stance in regards to being Pro-Life is that he supports the current status quo in regards to when a woman can abort. He also claimed he was entirely onboard for exceptions to the law for instances of rape, incest, and/or a danger to the life of the mother.

So to say he's "Pro-Life" is a bit of a misnomer, considering he has mentioned quite a bit in the past that he believes the procedure is something that he "believes it is a personal decision that should be left to the women and their doctors," to quote his AP interview on Dec 2, 1999. At best/worst, he is personally Pro-Life, but is open to allowing certain concessions to his personal viewpoints in the Law. I personally disagree with Mr. Trump on the Pro-Life position, from a conservative viewpoint, (I have written extensively on the topic in the past here for anyone who wishes to read more about how one can have both a conservative outlook and be Pro-Choice) but his position on the matter should be tolerable to people of both political stripes (Liberals because he doesn't want to restrict abortions any more than they already are, conservatives because he doesn't want taxpayer money to go to Planned Parenthood.)
